title: Risk Premium of the Preceding Term on a Backdated Cancellation — NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
On the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own), a cancellation whose effective date reaches back into or before the term before the current one also returns risk premium of that preceding term.

**Rule.** The risk premium of the term before the current one is settled as follows: when the cancellation effective date falls on or before the start of that term, it is returned in full; when the cancellation effective date falls within that term, it is returned for the days from the cancellation effective date to the current term start over the days of the current term; otherwise nothing is returned for it.

The preceding term's risk premium is the risk premium charges booked for that term apart from those of the policy's latest premium-bearing endorsement. The term before the current one ends at the current term start.

## Ladder

| Cancellation effective date | Preceding term's risk premium returned |
|---|---|
| on or before the start of the preceding term | in full |
| within the preceding term | days from the effective date to the current term start, over the days of the current term |
| on or after the current term start | nothing |

## Cases (hypothetical; current term 365 days, preceding-term risk premium 3,285.00)

- Effective 90 days before the current term start: 3,285.00 times 90 over 365 is 810.00.
- Effective on the first day of the preceding term: 3,285.00.
- Effective on the current term start: nothing from the preceding term.
